title: Quran Study from Behrouz 17: Suras 90, 91, 82, and 83 (1989-07-21)

cases.question: What kind of work does Quran 90:4 describe?
cases.expected_answer_note: Rashad reads Sura 90 and focuses on humanity being created to work hard for redemption. The difficult earthly condition is linked with the premortal offense, and the inability of some people to prostrate becomes an example of failed spiritual development. Every person remains accountable.

cases.question: Why was boasting about spending condemned?
cases.expected_answer_note: Quran 90:6–7 condemns boasting over money and assuming no one sees. Rashad emphasizes that provision comes only from God, cites Quran 29:17, and treats boastful expenditure as ego and idolatry when money or human providers replace God.

cases.question: Why were eyes, tongue, and lips mentioned?
cases.expected_answer_note: The study reflects on the design and purpose of eyes, tongue, and lips, then the two paths shown to humanity. The difficult path is paradoxically the route God makes easier for those who observe His commands, while the seemingly easy path leads to misery.

cases.question: Which actions make up the difficult path?
cases.expected_answer_note: Quran 90:13–20 defines the difficult path through freeing slaves, feeding during hardship, caring for related orphans and the needy, believing, and exhorting one another to steadfastness and kindness. These actions lead to happiness, while rejection leads to misery and confinement in Hell.

cases.question: What series of oaths opens Sura 91?
cases.expected_answer_note: Rashad studies the oaths by the sun, moon, day, night, sky, Earth, and soul. God shows the soul good and evil, and success depends on redeeming rather than neglecting it. Thamud follows its worst member, violates the camel test, and is annihilated.

cases.question: Which events open Sura 82?
cases.expected_answer_note: Edip reads Sura 82. The heavens shatter, planets scatter, oceans explode, graves open, and each soul learns what advanced or regressed it. Human design is presented as evidence against ingratitude. Invisible keepers record deeds, the righteous reach bliss, the wicked reach Hell, and all decisions belong to God.

cases.question: What conduct is condemned at the start of Sura 83?
cases.expected_answer_note: Sura 83 condemns people who demand full measure while cheating others. It asks whether they expect resurrection and describes the wicked record in Sijjeen as a numerically structured book. Persistent sin shields the heart and isolates rejecters from God.

cases.question: How is Elliyyeen described?
cases.expected_answer_note: The righteous record is placed in Elliyyeen, also translated as a numerically structured book, witnessed by those close to God. The righteous enjoy visible joy and special drink. Those mocked in worldly life laugh at the rejecters on Judgment Day, completing a reversal of ridicule.
